title: Apple Pay vanishes from Walmart app & website without explanation
summary: Walmart's love-hate relationship with Apple Pay continues, as the service has been removed from the Walmart iOS app, leaving it available only at in-person kiosks. Walmart has removed Apple Pay support from its website and iOS app. While Apple Pay launched in the United States all the way back in 2014, Walmart stood as one of its longest-running holdouts. The company forced shoppers to scan its own Walmart Pay QR codes instead, which allowed for greater insight into consumer habits. That was the case until August 2026 , when Walmart finally announced it would begin accepting Apple Pay at store locations in the United States. In October 2026, Apple Pay became available via the Walmart website and iOS app, but as of Tuesday, that's no longer the case. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

title: Claude can now turn artifacts into semi-independent Mac apps
summary: While a new Claude feature makes it seem like making a Mac app is now easier than ever, a major caveat means these AI-generated apps are worth avoiding altogether. Claude can now make Mac apps, though you'll still want to avoid them. Screenshot credit: Anthropic. While Apple itself has recognized the potential of AI-assisted software development, with Xcode 27 adding support for agentic coding, other companies have taken things further. Rather than an AI agent suggesting user interface layouts, Anthropic's Claude can now build macOS apps from prompts. In a press release on the Claude website, Anthropic revealed that its users can now "use Claude artifacts to create, run, and share desktop apps." Dubbed the "Install as app" feature, the capability is rolling out in beta for Claude users running macOS and Windows. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

title: National security, more affairs, and possible treason - Nvidia's problems are far from over
summary: Reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO is only the latest controversy surrounding Nvidia. It has not repaired Nvidia's reputational damage, and federal investigations that could see jail time will stretch on for years. Trump (left) pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated - image credits: White House, Nvidia. Trump said publicly that Jensen Huang did nothing wrong , and it was his intervention that made the Nvidia board reinstate the disgraced CEO despite its preference not to . However, two new reports detail just what Trump really felt, and precisely how Nvidia will remain in trouble. "The legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now [borne] by the board of Nvidia," Sen. Kevin Cramer (R., N.D.) has told the Wall Street Journal , "but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens." title: XNULinux can run macOS apps in Linux without a virtual machine
summary: The XNULinux project is able to run macOS 27 and macOS apps on a Linux PC, all without requiring any virtualization. It's still not bootable, though. Running macOS on Linux Most Linux projects AppleInsider writes about involve trying to run Linux on a Mac . However, there's now a project that is running macOS on Linux. Outside of building a Hackintosh, the usual way to run a macOS app on Linux or non-Apple hardware is through a virtual machine.
